frames.narration: Booking a trip spans three services, each with its own database. No single transaction can cover them, so the orchestrator runs a saga.
Step 1: reserve the flight. This is a normal local transaction and it commits at once.
Step 2: reserve the hotel, another local commit.
Step 3: charge the card. This time the payment is declined.
The flight and hotel are already committed, so they cannot simply be rolled back. The saga must undo them with compensating actions, in reverse order.
Compensation 1: cancel the hotel reservation (the most recent successful step).

Every service is back in a consistent state, without any distributed lock. Between the steps, though, other users could briefly have seen the seat and room as taken: that is the price of eventual consistency.
